latest_evidence.probe: Can deterministic effect-resource identity using standard HTTP PUT plus If-None-Match:* eliminate idempotency-key retention when the useful effect is exactly the addressed resource state, and where do hidden/non-resource side effects invalidate the equivalence?
latest_evidence.tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification using only frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local state and RFC 9110; no external effect, hosted compute, paid/trial API, protected authority, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, manual execution or quota-bearing service.
latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: A deterministic stable target resource plus PUT and If-None-Match:* can replace a separate idempotency-key registry only when the complete useful effect is exactly that durable resource state. The target identity is then the durable duplicate key and an ambiguous-success retry is blocked before method execution while the representation exists. The equivalence fails when the representation can disappear before retries are impossible, when the useful effect is not fully represented by that resource, or when hidden/non-resource side effects are not transactionally coupled to durable resource creation. PUT idempotence constrains intended effect, not every implementation side effect.
